title: Switchable day-trader timeframe mode (ch. 39) -- fully configurable, global setting
description: Ch. 39, 'Choosing Timeframes--the Factor of Five': Triple Screen doesn't hard-code weekly/daily/intraday -- it's built around whatever three timeframes the trader picks, each related to its neighbor by roughly a factor of five. This app currently hard-codes the swing/position-trader pairing (weekly/daily/intraday). Day-trading is the book's other explicit example (25-min/5-min/2-min, or a 39-min/8-min pairing). This is a genuinely large feature -- a new intraday data dependency (needs IBKR live, unlike everything else in this app which works via always-on yfinance), and a real architecture change everywhere the app currently assumes 'weekly'/'daily' as fixed concepts (schema field names, cache table interval columns, calendar-week truncation logic) rather than a generic long-term/intermediate/short-term triple. Product decisions (2026-09-24, by the user directly, see `decisions` below): build it; ship a fully user-configurable timeframe triple (not one of the book's fixed examples); make it a single global app-wide setting, not a per-request parameter. The checklist below is a first-pass breakdown of the work this implies -- given the scope, whoever picks this up should feel free to further split it into dependent sub-tasks (recording that as its own `decisions` entry) rather than trying to land it all in one PR.

checklist.step: Answer the questions below and move this task to 'planned' before any implementation work starts.

Design the generic timeframe-triple model that replaces the app's current hard-coded weekly/daily/intraday assumption: a long-term/intermediate/short-term triple of intervals, validated to roughly follow ch. 39's factor-of-five spacing (decide and record how strictly to enforce this -- a hard validation error vs. a soft warning vs. no enforcement at all, since ch. 39 itself frames the exact ratio as a guideline, not a hard rule). This needs to reach every place the app currently assumes 'weekly'/'daily' as fixed concepts: schema field names (app/api/schemas.py), the OHLCV cache table's interval column (app/data/cache.py), calendar-week truncation logic, and the signal engine's tide/wave/ripple evaluation (app/signals/engine.py).

Add a global app-wide setting (persisted, not per-request) storing the active trading mode (swing/position-trader vs. day-trader) and, when day-trader mode is active, the user-configured timeframe triple. Design the storage (a new settings table/row vs. extending an existing one) and the API surface to read/write it.

Wire IBKR live intraday data fetching for the short-term (and, if the configured triple's intermediate timeframe is also intraday, that one too) leg of the day-trader triple. Must degrade gracefully to a clear disabled/unavailable state (not an error) when IBKR isn't connected or FINTRADE_IBKR_ENABLED is false, consistent with every other IBKR-dependent feature's contract in this app (see backend-market-scanner/backend-market-breadth-indicators for the established pattern).

Adapt the signal engine's Triple Screen evaluation (tide/wave/ripple) to operate generically over whichever three timeframes are currently configured, instead of hard-coded weekly/daily/intraday -- this is the core methodology change; needs an elder-signal-reviewer pass given ch. 39's own framing of what changes and what stays invariant when timeframes shift (the Impulse System, confidence scoring, and 6% Rule risk logic should all remain timeframe-agnostic in principle -- confirm this holds, don't assume it).

Update API schemas/endpoints to expose the active mode and the generically-computed signals, decide whether existing weekly/daily-named response fields need renaming or can stay as aliases for whichever timeframe currently fills that role, and regenerate backend/openapi.json + frontend/src/api/types.ts.
Frontend: add a settings UI to view/switch the global trading mode and configure the day-trader timeframe triple.

Unit/integration tests for the generic timeframe evaluation (including a mocked IBKR intraday provider -- no test may make a live network call), the settings persistence/API, and frontend tests for the settings UI.
elder-signal-reviewer pass before merge (this changes core signal/methodology logic, not just plumbing).

decisions.rationale: The user was asked directly whether to build this given its scope (a real architecture change, not a UI toggle) and its hard IBKR-live dependency (unlike every other feature in this app). Chose to build it.

decisions.decision: Ship a fully user-configurable timeframe triple, not one of the book's fixed example triples (25-min/5-min/2-min or 39-min/8-min).
decisions.rationale: The user was asked to choose between the book's two fixed examples or a fully configurable triple. Chose configurable, matching ch. 39's own framing that timeframe choice is inherently personal to the trader, despite the higher implementation cost relative to a fixed pairing.

decisions.decision: Day-trader mode is a single global app-wide setting, not a per-analysis-request parameter.
decisions.rationale: The user was asked whether the whole app should switch mode at once (global) or whether a ticker could be viewed in either mode independently (per-request). Chose global -- a much smaller, less breaking API contract change than threading a mode parameter through every signal/analysis endpoint.

questions.question: Should day-trader timeframe mode be built at all, given its scope (a real architecture change, not just a UI toggle) and its hard dependency on IBKR being live (unlike every other feature in this app, which works with no IBKR setup)?
questions.context: This is a product/scope call, not something a worker can decide and record on its own -- it commits the app to maintaining a second, materially different data pipeline and a generic long/intermediate/short-term timeframe model throughout the signal engine and API schema. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): yes, build it -- see the decisions entry above.

questions.question: If built, which timeframe triple should ship first -- the book's 25-min/5-min/2-min example, its 39-min/8-min pairing (chosen because 39 minutes divides the 390-minute US trading day into a clean 10 bars), or a fully user-configurable triple?
questions.context: Each has different implementation cost: a fixed triple is far simpler than a configurable one, but ch.39 itself frames the timeframe choice as inherently personal to the trader. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): fully user-configurable -- see the decisions entry above.

questions.question: Should this be a global app-wide setting (the whole app switches mode) or a per-analysis-request parameter (a ticker can be viewed in either mode)?
questions.context: This changes the shape of the API contract change significantly -- a global setting is a much smaller, less breaking change than a per-request parameter threaded through every signal/analysis endpoint. ANSWERED (2026-09-24T15:13:24Z, by the user directly): global app-wide setting -- see the decisions entry above.
